codebook_title: Existential Analysis and Logotherapy 4 Fundamental Motivations (EA LT 4FMs) Codebook

source_documents.apa_citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers.
source_documents.summary: This article defines the four fundamental themes/conditions of existence (4FMs) as the cornerstones of existence that challenge a person to respond and activate inner freedom, serving as the basis for the fundamental existential motivations.

source_documents.apa_citation: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36.
source_documents.summary: This article further details the core existential motivations, their corresponding fundamental questions, their core concepts, and the objective (goal of dialogue) of successfully dealing with each motivation.

thematic_domains_4FMs.name: First Fundamental Motivation: The World—Dealing with Conditions and Possibilities
thematic_domains_4FMs.goal_of_dialogue: To achieve a fundamental 'Yes' to the conditions of existence and to achieve **Trust**.
thematic_domains_4FMs.goal_of_dialogue_justification: The goal in the dialogical process is to gain an acceptance of the existing conditions of life, to achieve a fundamental 'Yes' to the conditions of existence, and to achieve **Trust**[cite: 2].
thematic_domains_4FMs.definition_sub_theme: The first condition arises from the simple fact that I am here at all, that I am in the world[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_need_justification: Can I claim my place in this world under the conditions and with the possibilities I have? [cite_start]This demands three things: **protection, space and support**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.positive_outcome_justification: But if I do have these three things [protection, space, support], I will be able to feel **trust in the world and confidence in myself**, maybe even **faith in God**. [cite_start]The sum of these experiences of trust is the **fundamental trust**.... [cite: 1]
thematic_domains_4FMs.negative_pathology_justification: If this is not the case [protection, space, support are lacking], the result will be **restlessness, insecurity and fear**... If this is not the case, **psychodynamics takes over the guidance in the form of coping reactions**, which are to secure life[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.active_participation_justification: My active part in this fundamental condition of being there is to **accept** the positive sides and to **endure** the negative sides[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_example: Statements solely describing a 'reaction' or 'reflex' without personal decision/involvement.
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_justification: Without this involvement of the person in the motivational process, human beings would not be dealing with a question of motivation. [cite_start]Instead, there would be a sort of **reflex or reaction**, but no 'action'[cite: 1].

thematic_domains_4FMs.name: Second Fundamental Motivation: Life—Dealing with Relationships and Emotions
thematic_domains_4FMs.core_question_justification: I am alive—**do I like this fact**? [cite_start]Is it good to be there?[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.goal_of_dialogue: To achieve an essential 'Yes' to the values of existence and to achieve **Fundamental Value**.
thematic_domains_4FMs.goal_of_dialogue_justification: The goal in the dialogical process is to gain the feeling of the value of existence, to achieve an essential 'Yes' to the values of existence, and to achieve **Fundamental Value**[cite: 2].
thematic_domains_4FMs.definition_sub_theme: Once someone has his/her space in the world, he/she can fill it with life. Simply being there is not enough. We want our existence to be good, since it is more than a mere fact. [cite_start]It has a 'pathic dimension,' which means that we experience and suffer or enjoy it[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_need_justification: In order to seize my life, to love it, I need three things: **relationship, time and closeness**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.positive_outcome: Fundamental Value, Harmony, Depth of Life
thematic_domains_4FMs.positive_outcome_justification: But if these three conditions are fulfilled, I experience myself as being in **harmony** with the world and with myself, and I can sense the **depth of life**. [cite_start]These experiences form the **fundamental value**, the most profound feeling for the value of life[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.negative_pathology_justification: If relationships, closeness and time are lacking, **longing** will arise, then **coldness** and finally **depression**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.active_participation: Turning to (others/things/self), Consent to Being Touched (Feeling)
thematic_domains_4FMs.active_participation_justification: I seize life, engage in it, when I **turn to other people, to things**... when I go towards it, get close, get into touch or pull it towards me... If life is to make me move freely, my **consent to being touched (to feeling)** is necessary[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_example: Statements solely describing a 'reaction' or 'reflex' without personal decision/involvement.
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_justification: Without this involvement of the person in the motivational process, human beings would not be dealing with a question of motivation. [cite_start]Instead, there would be a sort of **reflex or reaction**, but no 'action'[cite: 1].

thematic_domains_4FMs.name: Third Fundamental Motivation: Being a Person—Dealing with Uniqueness and Conscience
thematic_domains_4FMs.core_question: Am I allowed to be like this?
thematic_domains_4FMs.core_question_justification: I am myself—**may I be like this**? Do I feel free to be like that? [cite_start]**Do I have the right to be what I am** and to behave as I do?[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.goal_of_dialogue: To achieve a structural 'Yes' to the value of the self and to achieve **Self-Esteem**.
thematic_domains_4FMs.goal_of_dialogue_justification: The goal in the dialogical process is to gain an acceptance of the Self, to achieve a structural 'Yes' to the value of the self, and to achieve **Self-Esteem**[cite: 2].
thematic_domains_4FMs.definition_sub_theme: In spite of my being related to life and to people, I am aware of my being separate, different. There is a singularity that makes me an 'I' and distinguishes me from everybody else. [cite_start]This is the plane of **identity, of knowing oneself and of ethics**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_need_justification: In order to succeed here [being a person], it is necessary to have experienced three things: **attention, justice and appreciation**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.positive_outcome_justification: If, on the contrary, these experiences have been made, I will find myself; find my **authenticity, my relief and my self-respect**. [cite_start]The sum of these experiences builds one’s own worth, the profoundest worth of what identifies my own self at its core: the **self-esteem**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.negative_pathology_result: Solitude, Hysteria, Need to Hide behind Shame
thematic_domains_4FMs.negative_pathology_justification: If these experiences are missing, **solitude** will be the result, **hysteria** as well as a **need to hide behind the shame**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.active_participation_justification: I also have to **say 'yes to myself'**. This requires my active participation: to look at other people, to **encounter** them and, at the same time, to **demarcate myself and to refuse** whatever does not correspond to me. [cite_start]**Encounter and regret** are the two means by which we can live our authenticity[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_example: Statements solely describing a 'reaction' or 'reflex' without personal decision/involvement.
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_justification: Without this involvement of the person in the motivational process, human beings would not be dealing with a question of motivation. [cite_start]Instead, there would be a sort of **reflex or reaction**, but no 'action'[cite: 1].

thematic_domains_4FMs.name: Fourth Fundamental Motivation: Meaning—Dealing with Becoming, Future and Commitment
thematic_domains_4FMs.core_question_justification: I am there—**for what is it good**?[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.goal_of_dialogue: To achieve a dynamic 'Yes' to meaning and to achieve **Fulfillment**.
thematic_domains_4FMs.goal_of_dialogue_justification: The goal in the dialogical process is to gain a dynamic 'Yes' to meaning, and to achieve **Fulfillment**[cite: 2].
thematic_domains_4FMs.definition_sub_theme: It does not suffice to simply be there and to have found oneself. In a sense, we have to **transcend ourselves**, if we want to find fulfillment and to be fruitful. [cite_start]This is the recognition of what my life is all about[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_need_set: Field of Activity, Structural Context, and Value to be realized in the Future
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_need_justification: For this, three things are necessary: a **field of activity, a structural context and a value to be realized in the future**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.positive_outcome: Sense of Fulfillment, Dedication, Action, Religious Belief
thematic_domains_4FMs.positive_outcome_justification: If, on the contrary, these conditions are met, I will be capable of **dedication and action** and, finally, of my own form of **religious belief**. [cite_start]The sum of these experiences adds up to the **meaning of life** and leads to a sense of **fulfillment**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.negative_pathology_result: Feeling of Emptiness, Frustration, Despair, Addiction
thematic_domains_4FMs.negative_pathology_justification: If this is not the case, the result will be a **feeling of emptiness, frustration, even despair and frequently addiction**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.active_participation: Openness (Phenomenological Attitude), Agreement with the Situation
thematic_domains_4FMs.active_participation_justification: The attitude of **openness** represents the existential access to meaning in life: i.e., dealing with the questions put before me in each situation... My active part in this attitude of openness is to bring myself into **agreement with the situation**[cite: 1].
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_example: Statements solely describing a 'reaction' or 'reflex' without personal decision/involvement.
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_justification: Without this involvement of the person in the motivational process, human beings would not be dealing with a question of motivation. [cite_start]Instead, there would be a sort of **reflex or reaction**, but no 'action'[cite: 1].
